Sam (Sales): heads up — Acme POC ramped this morning. They're seeing slow cold TTFT on chat ops and hit a couple 429s. Also asking for a pricing note for burst vs reserved. @Alex @Maya can you help triage?
Alex (Eng Runtime): on it. can you paste a sample request/headers and approx tokens?
Sam (Sales): single-turn chat, ~6 prompt tokens + ~200 gen tokens. curl we got from their dev:
Sam (Sales): ```curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme\" -d '{"model":"rwkv-13b","input":"summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate```
Maya (Eng ML): quick questions: are they using streaming? did they pin model variant?
Sam (Sales): streaming enabled. not pinned (default).
Alex (Eng Runtime): got logs for that API key — high prefix cache miss rate (~87%) and lots of 1-request batches. Also saw batching window set to 50ms for their client by default. That combo increases TTFT for small single-user interactive flows.
Alex (Eng Runtime): short repro of observed behavior: 1) request arrives, 2) runtime waits batch_window (50ms) trying to coalesce, 3) only one request in batch => kernel overhead dominates => TTFT ~180-240ms. With streaming handshake adds ~40ms.
Maya (Eng ML): also model quantization variant fallback: they're on default-32 which is heavier. If they used fast-8bit variant we see ~20-30% per-token latency drop.
Elena (Solutions): pricing question: they want clear delta between on-demand bursts vs reserved. Sam — they want a bullet we can share asap.
Sam (Sales): yes. need both: "short-term POC bursts" and "monthly reserved slot" numbers.
Alex (Eng Runtime): immediate mitigation we can ask client to try: 1) set batch_window_ms=10, 2) set max_batch_size=8, 3) enable prefix KV cache (client should send conversation id as cache_key). Example config snippet:
Alex (Eng Runtime): ```json
{
  "batching": {"batch_window_ms": 10, "max_batch_size": 8},
  "caching": {"enabled": true, "cache_key": "conversation_id"},
  "model": "rwkv-13b-fast-8bit"
}
```
Maya (Eng ML): adding: enable streaming chunks of 64 tokens so downstream latency feels faster for user. That helps perceived TTFT.
Sam (Sales): can we also explain the 429s? they hit them after a few minutes of high concurrency.
Alex (Eng Runtime): 429s look like client-side rate limit (token-level quotas) — headers show x-rdwd-rl-remaining low. We can temporarily bump their project quota for the POC (sandbox) or recommend exponential backoff with Retry-After header handling.
ops-bot: Deploy finished: routing update to us-east-2 completed at 1765123600.
Maya (Eng ML): one more note on cache: their current client builds slightly different prompt prefixes per message (timestamps included) -> cache misses. Recommend stable system prompts and canonicalize user metadata outside the prompt.
Elena (Solutions): pricing bullets for Sam: "On-demand (POC bursts): billed per-token, nominal extra for burst capacity; estimate during POC: ~ $0.06 / 1k gen tokens at this model/variant. Reserved slots: monthly commit gives ~40-55% discount and predictable latency SLOs. I'll follow up with exact numbers from finance."
Sam (Sales): great — pls send exact reserved SKU numbers when you have them. For now I'll ask Acme to try Alex's config and canonicalize prompts.
Alex (Eng Runtime): action items: 1) I'll temp bump their sandbox quota for 24h. 2) I'll open a short-lived canary with fast-8bit variant in us-east-2 and drop a test endpoint for them. 3) leave tracing hooks so we can correlate request_id -> batch sizes.
Maya (Eng ML): I'll add an eval snippet to measure TTFT before/after and share a 2-min doc.
Sam (Sales): timeline: ask Acme to test changes in next 2 hours. I'll send pricing note and security checklist entries they asked for.
Alex (Eng Runtime): quick repro commands for them to run locally:
Alex (Eng Runtime): ```bash
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rwkv-13b-fast-8bit","input":"short prompt","stream":true,"conversation_id":"acme-demo-1"}' \
  https://api.us-east-2.redwood.company/v1/generate
```
Sam (Sales): got it. I'll coordinate. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Elena (Solutions): ping me if they ask for SOC2 entries — I can attach the snippet.
Alex (Eng Runtime): follow-up: I bumped quota at 1765123620, canary endpoint is live 1765123645. I'll watch for batch size distribution and post results.
Sam (Sales): updated — Acme ran tests at 1765123700 and reported median TTFT dropped from ~220ms to ~95ms. They also saw far fewer 429s after the quota bump.
Maya (Eng ML): nice. keep me posted if any quality regressions with fast-8bit.
Alex (Eng Runtime): closing loop: I'll roll recommended config into a POC checklist template so future deals don't repeat this.
Sam (Sales): perfect. I'll update the deal notes and send the pricing draft.
Elena (Solutions): will follow with reserved pricing SKUs and SOC2 checklist items.
Sam (Sales): thanks all — great swarm! :party:
